name: claude agents
description: Open agent view to monitor and dispatch parallel background sessions.

examples.explanation: List and monitor background sessions.
Show only sessions started under one directory.

when_to_use: See which background sessions exist and dispatch new ones.

name: claude attach
description: Open a background session in this terminal by its short id.

examples.explanation: Bring a background session into this terminal.

when_to_use: Take over a session started with --bg.

name: claude logs
description: Print recent terminal output from a background session.

examples.explanation: Read a background session's recent output.

when_to_use: Check on a background run without attaching to it.

name: claude respawn
description: Restart a background session, running or stopped, with its conversation intact.

examples.explanation: Restart one background session on the current version.
Restart every running session to pick up an update.

when_to_use: Move running sessions onto a newly installed Claude Code version.

name: claude stop
description: Stop a background session while keeping its conversation.

examples.explanation: Stop a background session and keep its transcript.

when_to_use: Halt background work without discarding the conversation.
when_not_to_use: It does not delete the session; use claude rm for that.

name: claude rm
description: Remove a background session from the list, and its worktree when that is safe.

examples.explanation: Delete a finished background session.

when_to_use: Clear out sessions that have already exited.
when_not_to_use: The transcript stays on the local machine and remains available through claude --resume.

name: claude auth
description: Command group for signing in, signing out, and inspecting authentication state.

examples.explanation: Check whether this machine is signed in.

when_to_use: Manage credentials from the shell rather than from a session.

name: claude auth status
description: Show authentication status as JSON, exiting 0 when logged in and 1 when not.

examples.explanation: Print authentication status as JSON.

examples.command: claude auth status --text || claude auth login
examples.explanation: Gate a script on being signed in.

when_to_use: Check credentials in CI before starting a run.

name: claude setup-token
description: Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts, printed to the terminal without being saved.

examples.explanation: Print a long-lived token for a CI secret store.

when_to_use: Authenticate an automated environment that cannot run a browser flow.

name: claude auto-mode
description: Command group for inspecting or resetting the auto mode classifier configuration.

examples.explanation: Show the effective auto mode configuration.

when_to_use: Understand why auto mode is or is not approving an action.

name: claude auto-mode config
description: Print the effective auto mode configuration with your settings applied.

examples.explanation: See the auto mode rules actually in force.

when_to_use: Compare your customized rules against the built-in defaults.

name: claude auto-mode defaults
description: Print the built-in auto mode classifier rules as JSON.

examples.explanation: Print the shipped classifier rules.

when_to_use: Read the baseline before writing your own auto mode rules.

name: claude auto-mode critique
description: Inspect auto mode classifier behavior for a candidate rule set.

examples.explanation: Inspect classifier behavior for the current rules.

when_to_use: Check custom auto mode rules before relying on them.
notes: Exposed by the 2.1.261 binary; the CLI reference documents auto-mode defaults and reset but not this subcommand.

name: claude auto-mode reset
description: Restore the default auto mode configuration by removing the autoMode section from user settings.

examples.explanation: Drop custom auto mode rules and return to defaults.

when_to_use: Recover from auto mode rules that approve or block the wrong actions.
when_not_to_use: It edits your user settings file; it prompts for confirmation before writing.

name: claude mcp
description: Configure and manage Model Context Protocol servers from the shell.

examples.explanation: List the configured MCP servers.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
examples.explanation: Add an HTTP MCP server.

when_to_use: Add, inspect, or remove MCP servers without opening a session.

name: claude mcp login
description: Run a configured MCP server's OAuth flow without opening the interactive /mcp panel.

examples.explanation: Complete a server's OAuth flow from the shell.

when_to_use: Authenticate an HTTP, SSE, or claude.ai connector server outside a session.

name: claude mcp logout
description: Clear stored OAuth credentials for an MCP server.

examples.explanation: Remove stored credentials for one server.

when_to_use: Revoke a server's stored credentials on a shared machine.

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.1.186 or later.

name: claude plugin
description: Command group for installing, enabling, inspecting, and removing Claude Code plugins.

examples.explanation: List installed plugins.
Check a plugin before installing it.

when_to_use: Manage plugins from the shell rather than the interactive /plugin manager.

name: claude project
description: Command group for managing Claude Code's local state for a project.

examples.explanation: Delete local Claude Code state for this project.

when_to_use: Clean up or inspect the local state Claude Code keeps for a repository.

name: claude project purge
description: Delete all local Claude Code state for a project: transcripts, task lists, debug logs, file-edit history, and prompt history.

examples.explanation: Remove local state for the current project.

when_to_use: Hand over a machine, or clear state after working on sensitive code.
when_not_to_use: It is destructive and removes transcripts that resume depends on.

name: claude doctor
description: Print read-only installation and settings diagnostics without starting a session.

examples.explanation: Check install health and settings validity from the shell.

when_to_use: Diagnose a broken install or an invalid settings file.
when_not_to_use: For a full checkup that can also fix issues, run /doctor inside a session.

name: claude install
description: Install or reinstall the native binary, optionally pinning a version.

examples.explanation: Install the native build.
Pin a specific version.

when_to_use: Move between released versions, or repair an installation.

name: claude update
description: Check for updates and install a newer version if one is available.

examples.explanation: Update to the latest version.

when_to_use: Pick up a newer release before starting long-running work.

name: claude import
description: Start a session that imports configuration from another AI coding agent into Claude Code.

examples.explanation: Bring Codex configuration into Claude Code.

when_to_use: Migrate from another agent without rewriting configuration by hand.

name: claude gateway
description: Start the self-hosted Claude apps gateway server for administrators deploying SSO and policy.

examples.explanation: Start the enterprise auth and telemetry gateway.

when_to_use: Deploy SSO and policy in front of Claude Code for an organization.
when_not_to_use: This is an administrator surface, not part of an ordinary coding session.

name: claude remote-control
description: Start a Remote Control server so Claude Code can be driven from claude.ai or the Claude app.

examples.explanation: Run in server mode for remote steering.

when_to_use: Continue or steer a local session from another device.
when_not_to_use: It runs in server mode and does not start a local interactive session.

name: claude self-hosted-runner
description: Register this machine or container with a self-hosted environment and host Claude Code cloud sessions on your own infrastructure.

examples.explanation: Host cloud sessions on your own infrastructure.

when_to_use: Run cloud sessions inside your own network or compliance boundary.

name: claude daemon
description: Command group for inspecting and stopping the background-session supervisor.

examples.explanation: Check the background-session supervisor.

when_to_use: Diagnose background sessions that will not start or attach.

name: claude daemon status
description: Print the background-session supervisor's state, version, socket directory, and worker count.

examples.explanation: Inspect the supervisor for diagnostics.

when_to_use: Confirm the supervisor is running before debugging background sessions.
when_not_to_use: It exits 1 when the supervisor is not running, which scripts should expect.

name: claude daemon stop
description: Stop the background-session supervisor and the sessions it hosts.

examples.explanation: Stop the supervisor and its hosted sessions.
Leave background sessions running for the next supervisor.

when_to_use: Restart supervision cleanly after an upgrade.

name: claude ultrareview
description: Run a cloud-hosted multi-agent code review of the current branch, a PR number, or a base branch, and print the findings.

examples.explanation: Review the current branch and print findings.
Review a pull request and emit the raw payload.

when_to_use: Run a deep review from a script or a CI job.
when_not_to_use: It exits 0 on success and 1 on failure, which reports the run rather than the review verdict.

name: --brief
description: Enable the SendUserMessage tool so the agent can send messages to the user during a run.

examples.explanation: Let the agent message the user directly during a run.

when_to_use: Follow a long unattended run through progress messages.

name: --file
description: Download file resources at startup, given as file_id:relative_path pairs.

examples.explanation: Fetch files into the session at startup.

when_to_use: Seed a session with files stored outside the working tree.

name: --permission-prompts
description: Choose where permission prompts are answered: host, or none.

examples.explanation: Run without routing permission prompts to a host.

when_to_use: Control how approvals surface when embedding Claude Code in another tool.

name: --system-prompt-snapshot
description: Turn system prompt snapshotting on or off for the session.

examples.explanation: Disable system prompt snapshots.

when_to_use: Control whether the resolved system prompt is captured for inspection.

name: --help
description: Print usage, options, and the available subcommands.

examples.explanation: List every option and subcommand.
List one subcommand group's own subcommands.

when_to_use: Check the exact surface of the installed build, including options the docs omit.

name: claude mcp add
description: Add an MCP server over stdio, SSE, or HTTP transport.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
examples.explanation: Add an HTTP server.

examples.command: claude mcp add my-server -e API_KEY=xxx -- npx my-mcp-server
examples.explanation: Add a stdio server with an environment variable.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http corridor https://app.corridor.dev/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer ..."
examples.explanation: Add an HTTP server that needs an auth header.

when_to_use: Register a server without editing configuration files by hand.
when_not_to_use: Review a server's command, URL, environment, and exposed tools before adding it; MCP tools act outside the repository.

name: claude mcp add-json
display_name: Add an MCP server from JSON
description: Add an MCP server from a JSON configuration string.

examples.explanation: Add a server from a JSON definition.

when_to_use: Script server registration, or copy a definition from another machine.

name: claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop
description: Import MCP servers already configured in Claude Desktop.

examples.explanation: Import Claude Desktop's configured servers.

when_to_use: Reuse servers you already trust in Claude Desktop.

conditions: Available on macOS and WSL only.

name: claude mcp get
description: Show the configuration of a single MCP server.

examples.explanation: Inspect one server's configuration.

when_to_use: Confirm a server's transport, scope, and command before debugging it.

name: claude mcp list
description: List the configured MCP servers and their connection state.

examples.explanation: List configured servers.

when_to_use: Check which servers a project actually loads.

name: claude mcp remove
description: Remove a configured MCP server, optionally from a specific scope.

examples.explanation: Remove a server.
Remove it from the project scope only.

when_to_use: Drop a server you no longer trust or need.

name: claude mcp reset-project-choices
description: Clear the approval choices recorded for project-scoped MCP servers.

examples.explanation: Ask again about this project's servers.

when_to_use: Re-review project servers after a repository changes hands.

name: claude mcp serve
display_name: Serve Claude Code as an MCP server
description: Run Claude Code itself as an MCP server so another client can use its tools.

examples.explanation: Expose Claude Code's tools over MCP.
Serve with debug output while diagnosing a client.

when_to_use: Let another MCP client drive Claude Code's tools.

name: --transport
description: Transport for an MCP server: stdio, sse, or http. Defaults to stdio.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
examples.explanation: Register an HTTP server.

when_to_use: Register a remote server rather than a local child process.

name: --scope
description: Configuration scope for an MCP server: local, user, or project. Defaults to local.

examples.command: claude mcp add --scope project my-server -- npx my-mcp-server
examples.explanation: Share a server with everyone who clones the repository.

when_to_use: Decide whether a server travels with the repository or stays on your machine.

name: --env
description: Set environment variables for a stdio MCP server.

examples.command: claude mcp add my-server -e API_KEY=xxx -- npx my-mcp-server
examples.explanation: Pass a credential to a stdio server.

when_to_use: Supply configuration a stdio server reads from its environment.

name: --header
description: Set headers for HTTP or SSE MCP servers.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http corridor https://app.corridor.dev/api/mcp -H "X-Api-Key: abc123"
examples.explanation: Authenticate to a remote server with a header.

when_to_use: Reach a remote server that authenticates with a static header.

name: --client-id
description: OAuth client ID for HTTP or SSE MCP servers.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http acme https://mcp.acme.dev --client-id abc123
examples.explanation: Register a server with a pre-issued OAuth client.

when_to_use: Connect to a server that requires a registered OAuth client.

name: --client-secret
description: Prompt for an OAuth client secret rather than passing it on the command line.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http acme https://mcp.acme.dev --client-id abc123 --client-secret
examples.explanation: Enter the secret at a prompt instead of in shell history.

when_to_use: Keep a client secret out of your shell history.
notes: The secret can also be supplied through the MCP_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable.

name: --callback-port
description: Use a fixed port for the OAuth callback, for servers that require a pre-registered redirect URI.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http acme https://mcp.acme.dev --callback-port 8123
examples.explanation: Match a server's registered redirect URI.

when_to_use: Satisfy a server that only accepts a fixed redirect URI.
